business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bulk Dehydrated Garlic Flakes and Crushed Chili Pepper Export

stage_1.document_name: Certified true copies of passport/identity documents of each founder, UBO and director
stage_1.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority of the country of origin
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille in the issuing jurisdiction (Switzerland is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961); consular legalization where the origin state is not a Hague member

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620–659 (Aktiengesellschaft formation and capital), Art. 640 (share subscription), Art. 643 (board election), Art. 716a (non-transferable board duties); Federal Act on Commercial Register and Companies (HRegV) for filing procedure
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), consolidated in the Federal Commercial Register (ZEFIX) via the Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (Errichtungserklärung) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000; at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up in cash and placed at the free disposal of the board, evidenced by a bank confirmation issued after the capital is deposited on a blocked account opened in the company's name; capital retained in the company is prohibited (Kapitalaufbringung principle).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. That the Board acknowledges the subscription of 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 nominal each, entirely entitled to dividend. 2. That the registered office of the Company shall be established at Bundesstrasse 10, Zug, and any branch addresses are approved. 3. That the following officers are appointed: [Name], Chair and Chief Executive Officer; [Name], Secretary; [Name], Compliance and Finance Officer, each with authority to act severally. 4. That the directors are authorized to open a blocked bank account, deposit paid-up capital, execute commercial register filings, and publish SHAB notice. 5. That the accounting year closes 31 December and first audit is waived subject to statutory thresholds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Incorporation Deed and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Canton of Zug (Öffentliches Notariat)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association in German, setting out corporate name, registered office, purpose (wholesale trade in dehydrated vegetables and spices), share capital, and share classes. Convene the constitutive meeting; all initial shareholders appear before the notary to execute the deed and subscribe the shares. Obtain notarized originals for the subsequent registry filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (Statuten) in German
Notarized incorporation deed with share subscription list
Valid passports or ID cards of all initial shareholders
Certificate of domicile for the registered office (Handelsregisterbestätigung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry queries the deed, amend the articles and re-execute the notarial signature; material defects may be cured by a supplemental notary deed without repeating the entire formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Paid-in Capital Account and Deposit of Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss-regulated bank licensed by FINMA (Zug branch)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked corporate bank account (Sperrkonto) in the exact company name and legal form. Deposit at least CHF 50,000 of the aggregate subscription amount into the account. Obtain a bank capital confirmation letter (Freigabebestätigung) certifying that the funds are at the free disposal of the board and that no restrictions or liens exist.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed and Articles of Association
Passport or ID of the individual with signatory power
Beneficial ownership declaration (üconomikoy) and source-of-funds form
Bank account application and signature cards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests supplementary KYC evidence, provide beneficial owner registry extracts (e.g., registered office certificate and shareholder declarations) and resubmit; delayed deposit may be remedied by using a Swiss escrow agent for capital blocking.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (administrative seat at registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural board meeting, adopt the formal first board resolution, and record the following appointments: Chair/CEO, corporate secretary, and compliance/finance officer. Determine the signatory regime in accordance with the Articles; for an AG a two-person collective signature is presumed unless single authority is expressly granted. Decide on the audit opt-out by shareholders' resolution if statutory thresholds are not exceeded.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed
Shareholder subscription list
First board resolution minutes (Pro-Forma Board Resolution)
Written acceptance of office by each director
Audit opt-out declaration if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director refuses to serve or fails to meet Swiss residence requirements, remove or replace the affected officer by immediate shareholders' decision and amend the filing package before submission to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Legal Personality Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, the Articles, the board resolution, the bank capital confirmation, and the signed declarations of all directors through the official ZEFIX electronic portal or in paper form. Pay the registration fee and await the registrar's substantive audit of legality (Rechtsprüfung). Upon approval, the company is entered into the commercial register and obtains legal personality effective as of the date of entry.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed
Articles of Association with certified signatures
Bank capital confirmation (Freigabebestätigung)
First board resolution with officer appointments
Signed director acceptance declarations
Cantonal and federal fee payment receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query or provisional rejection, respond in writing within ten days with corrected documents and clarifications; for missing Swiss-domiciled director declarations, submit replacement evidence and reapply; any refusal may be appealed to the Cantonal Superior Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in Swiss Official Gazette and Post-Registration Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Commercial Gazette (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB) and Cantonal Tax/Food Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the registry transmits the new entry to the SHAB for official publication. Obtain certified commercial register extracts from ZEFIX. Register for value added tax (VAT) if annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, for social security as an employer, and with the Cantonal Company Tax Office for direct tax purposes. If physical food storage or handling is intended, file the food business registration with the cantonal food control authority.
required_dossiers: Certified commercial register extract (ZEFIX)
VAT registration form (Formulaire 1300)
Tax registration questionnaire for Zug
Employer register form for social security (AHV)
Food business registration form, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication is incorrect, request a corrective publication from the registry administration; if tax or food registrations are deficient, resubmit the required forms through the cantonal online services and maintain proof of submission to avoid penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Food Control Authority of Zug (Amt für Lebensmittelkontrolle) under the technical supervision of the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO / BLV); for any processing, the Cantonal Office for Trade and Industry (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operating Licence / Betriebsbewilligung (for wholesale trading, storage, and repacking of dehydrated vegetables, garlic flakes, and crushed chili pepper)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU / FOEN) and the Cantonal Office for the Environment of Zug (Umweltschutz-Amt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal EIA classification; however, a low-risk environmental registration may be required if the facility includes repacking, dust-generating processing, or waste storage exceeding VVEA thresholds. A full EIA is not required for pure commodity trading and storage of dried vegetables.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sewer: pH 6.5–8.5; COD ≤500 mg/L; TSS ≤300 mg/L; oil and grease ≤20 mg/L; VOC emissions from cleaning and dust-handling processes ≤0.5 g/m³; organic dust control to prevent explosibility; waste handling and recovery per Federal Ordinance on Movements of Waste (VVEA) and federal packaging recycling regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cantonal Fire Service (Feuerpolizei) with an approved fire extinguishing and evacuation plan; structural load inspection of storage racks by a licensed Swiss engineer; occupational health clearance per SUVA requirements, including dust protection, noise assessment, and first-aid measures; workplace signage in German/French/Italian as required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung / Administration fédérale des contributions), SWISS-TAX / SuiteTax portal (www.estv.admin.ch; VAT registration via SuiteTax e-Services).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Aktiengesellschaft is a distinct legal person subject to federal, cantonal, and communal corporate income tax; no pass-through status is available for an AG; territorial scope: Swiss-source and worldwide income with comprehensive taxation for resident corporations, subject to participation exemption and treaty relie)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, exercising monetary and statistical functions, with the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) regulating banking conduct and anti-money laundering compliance; trade sanctions and export-control administration fall under the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland applies a fully liberalized and freely convertible currency regime: the CHF floats under a flexible exchange-rate policy without capital or current account restrictions, so trade settlements, dividend distributions, equity injections, and loan repayments are entirely convertible without central bank approvals. The sole material profit-remittance hurdle is the statutory 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividends, generally reduced to 0–15% under double taxation treaties; no FX repatriation timing or amount limits exist.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion obligation exists in Switzerland. The AG may retain 100% of dehydrated vegetable and spice export receipts indefinitely in CHF or any foreign currency. Only balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the SNB applies for direct investment and payment stream data; non-conversion is free of penalty.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as supplementary treasury rail, Low as primary banking counterparty: FINMA-licensed fintech institutions (innovation-technology license under Art. 1b Swiss Banking Act) can hold public deposits up to CHF 100 million and execute payments, but they cannot provide full documentary trade finance (LC confirmation/advising) or investment-grade services. Non-Swiss EEA EMIs require their own FINMA authorization or branch presence, limiting their utility for the AG's LC and MT103 commodity-export flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not a legal mandate: FINMA permits compliant video-identification for AML purposes, and the AG's Low_Risk_Standard classification positions it favorably for remote onboarding. In practice, most tier-1 Swiss banks require one formal KYC interview — either in-person in Zurich/Geneva or via a FINMA-certified video call — involving at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner(s), supplemented by notarized corporate documents and a professional reference from an existing regulated bank or Swiss fiduciary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face identification of UBOs and directors with non-resident addresses
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled passports of all directors and UBOs; recent utility or bank statement for address proof; certified Handelsregister extract; notarized Articles of Association; board resolution for account opening; professional reference letter from a regulated bank or independent Swiss fiduciary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags: over/under-invoicing of bulk dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper shipments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete shipment file: signed purchase contract with Incoterms, commercial invoice, packing list, weight certificate, bill of lading/CMR, certificate of origin, Swiss customs export declaration, phytosanitary certificate, and independent commodity price benchmarks (e.g., Mintec/AGRI indices) demonstrating arm's-length wholesale pricing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, embargo, and end-use ambiguity for food-commodity export destinations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Positive-negative sanctions screening outputs (UN, EU, OFAC, SECO, FAFIF), end-user certificate from the overseas buyer, final-destination declaration, embargo compliance letter, and a client adequacy file confirming the buyer is an established wholesale spice importer with third-party trade references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth gaps on inbound equity injection funding the AG's minimum capital and working base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements of the shareholder/parent; corporate tax assessments or tax clearance certificates; bank reference letters from the remitting institution; board-approved treasury resolution explaining the commercial purpose; and a traceable funds trail from the beneficial owner's account into the Swiss AG's blocked capital contribution account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the AG's blocked capital contribution account (Sperrkonto) at a licensed Swiss bank, with payment narrative 'CAPITAL INJECTION / EQUITY CONTRIBUTION' and statistical classification as direct investment for SNB balance-of-payments reporting; CHF clearing executes via SIC, EUR via SEPA/T2, USD via US correspondent banks. Verification bundle: notarial deed of capital increase, bank receipt confirmation, Handelsregister post-registration extract, and shareholder remittance instructions retained for audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: SWIFT MT103/MT202 for direct T/T wire settlements to overseas spice buyers; commercial letters of credit (UCP 600, SWIFT MT700/MT707) with confirming banks for secured exports to emerging-market counterparties; documentary collections via MT798/SCF as secondary method; CHF settled through SIC, EUR through SEPA/TARGET2, USD through CHIPS/Fedwire correspondent networks. Each disbursement references contract and invoice numbers in SWIFT field 70, with underlying trade documentation (LC, bills of lading, certificates of origin) retained for compliance review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forward contracts (spot to 12-month tenors) in CHF/EUR/USD hedging invoice receivables, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or the Swiss bank's standard forward framework with board-approved treasury authorization
Cross-currency swaps / FX swaps for managing long-dated USD purchase commitments and rebalancing CHF base currency exposure against USD-denominated export offtake contracts
FX options and zero-cost collars designated as cash-flow hedges for commercial foreign-exchange risk under IFRS 9 hedge accounting

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) legally permissible but not market-required for CHF due to full convertibility; employed only where the counterparty cannot execute bilateral CHF settlement, referencing the European Central Bank's CHF fixing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and director's report approved by the Annual General Meeting (AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained at company's place of business; filed with Cantonal Tax Administration as part of tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of balance sheet date (e.g., by 30 June if 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government penalty; failure to comply permits shareholders to demand judicial review; continued non-filing may trigger insolvency proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cantonal and Federal Direct Corporate Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) / Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 3–6 months after annual financial statements are approved; most cantons require filing by 30 June for calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment and filing interest at statutory rate; default on filing results in assessment of CHF 100–500 fine and estimated tax levy; severe cases subject to criminal tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the tax period (annual filing available for turnover below CHF 5,005,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest of 4.75% per annum on arrears; administrative fine up to CHF 8,000; concealment of turnover attracts criminal penalty equal to unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register update for changes resolved at the AGM (directors, signatory powers, registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 14 days from the event (shall be registered without delay after AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Coercive fines (Ordnungsbusse) and administrative sanctions; inaccurate registration triggers liability for reliance damages and criminal sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full statutory audit required if, for two consecutive financial years, an AG exceeds two of: balance sheet total CHF 20 million, sales revenue CHF 40 million, 250 FTE employees; a limited audit (review) is required for companies with more than 10 FTE, or upon shareholder request (10% capital). No audit can be waived (shareholder opt-out) if the company qualifies as small and an ordinary or limited audit is not required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-960a); Swiss GAAP FER for large/audited entities; IFRS permitted for consolidated or listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law requires continuous updates to the register of members (Aktienbuch) and the register of directors, but there is no annual centralized UBO filing. Under anti-money laundering rules, the financial intermediary must verify ongoing UBO status at business inception and upon material transaction changes; not on an annual statutory calendar.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders and Board Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% (federal corporate income tax rate; combined cantonal/communal headline for a standard Zug-domiciled AG approximates 12.3%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general federal tax holiday. Cantonal/communal profit tax reductions apply in certain jurisdictions (e.g., Zug, Schwyz). Participation deduction exempts qualifying dividend and capital gain income. Patent box regime permits preferential deduction for eligible IP income (federal and cantonal). R&D superseded deduction of up to 150% for qualifying research activities. Ordinary and residual Swiss effective rates depend on pre-tax profit mix and location

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales (annual corporate tax return). Filed electronically via the Swiss Federal Tax Administration eTax portal or cantonal e-filing systems (e.g., taxonline Zug) except where mandatory paper filing still applies
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the company's financial year-end unless the cantonal tax administration grants an extension. For calendar-year taxpayers, the return is generally due by 30 June of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Profit and loss result (Résultat du compte de pertes et profits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the net commercial profit before taxes as per the company's statutory financial statements (Swiss GAAP or IFRS). This is the starting point for taxable profit determination.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident wholly owned AG, use the Swiss statutory accounts. Consolidate all worldwide income attributable to the Swiss permanent establishment; ensure no foreign permanent establishment income is incorrectly excluded without treaty exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Participations and capital gains (Déclarations des participations)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State income from qualifying participations (dividends, capital gains on shares) and claim the participation deduction where a 10% or greater shareholding is held and the conditions of Art. 69 LIFD are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent groups must attach detailed schedules proving 10% holding, holding period, and the participation deduction computation. For international holding structures, ensure no hybrid mismatch causes double non-taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim the offset of prior-year tax losses against current-year taxable income. The maximum carryforward period is 7 years under federal and cantonal law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an AG owned from abroad, losses may be used only to the extent the company still has an actual business in Switzerland; loss importing via restructuring may be attacked under anti-abuse rules. Attach loss carryforward statements and ownership continuity evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Additions and adjustments (Modifications apportées au résultat déclaré)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report hidden reserve adjustments, non-deductible expenses (taxes, penalties, excessive interest), and transfer pricing adjustments to align reported profit with arm's length standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must scrutinize related-party financing and provisioning to avoid downstream TP adjustments. Visible subordination and equity-to-debt ratios apply to prevent thin capitalization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim a credit or refund of the 35% Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends, interest on bonds, and similar income already subject to withholding in Switzerland.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Form 1085 accompanies the return. A foreign owner must prove that the Swiss tax withheld has actually been borne and that the economic beneficiary is the owner. The refund is granted only if the recipient qualifies under the DTA and domestic substance rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and incomplete filings trigger Ordnungsbusse (procedural fines) up to CHF 10,000 per instance. Any understated tax gives rise to interest at 3.5% per annum from the due date. Negligent or wilful evasion leads to tax evasion penalties of up to three times the evaded tax and potential criminal sanction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from reduced domestic or treaty withholding rates, the recipient must submit Form 823 (for relief at source) or Form 824 (for refund after deduction) to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA). A valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the recipient's country of residence, a shareholding and holding period certificate, and a dividend ownership declaration are mandatory. The FTA will approve the reduced rate under the applicable double tax treaty (typically 0–15% depending on ownership level and treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% statutory Swiss withholding tax (no WHT on IP licensing income). Interest: 35% anticipatory tax applies only to interest from bonds and money market paper; ordinary trade interest between companies is free from WHT. Under Swiss DTAs, treaty rates for interest range between 0% and 10%, and most modern treaties provide a 0% rate for arm's length interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF 50,000,000 (consolidated group revenue) and CHF 5,000,000 (gross related-party transactions) serve as the mandatory thresholds for a Local File and Master File; CbCR applies at CHF 5,000,000,000 group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not maintain separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as in the Gulf States, but an economic substance requirement is enforced through general anti-avoidance rules, treaty entitlement criteria (OECD BEPS/MLI), and the Swiss practice governing tax rulings. To retain fiscal domicile and treaty benefits, the CH_AG must maintain real presence in Switzerland: registered office, actual board control, operational personnel, adequate equipment, books and records, and substantive commercial decision-making. A pure paper company with no economic activity in Switzerland is liable to be denied tax residence and treaty relief, with assets subject to seizure and the company exposed to restructuring or liquidation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately filing false corporate returns by understating gross turnover, inflating deductible expenses, transferring profit through artificial intercompany invoices for dehydrated vegetable purchases, or concealing Swiss bank deposits from private banking relationships.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to three times the evaded tax (Art. 175 LIFD); in serious cases imprisonment up to three years (Art. 176 LIFD). Interest on unpaid tax plus late penalties accrue regardless of criminal sanction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign and approve inaccurate tax returns are liable for restitution of underpaid federal, cantonal, and communal taxes; enforcement can include travel bans and seizure of personal assets. Criminal prosecution under Swiss criminal law may result in custodial sentences for wilful bookkeeping omissions or involvement in fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG solely as a mail-drop entity with no physical office, no employees, no local management decisions, and no actual oversight of the dehydrated spices trading business, while attempting to claim Swiss treaty benefits, ruling exemptions, or tax amnesty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may disregard the legal form and allocate income to the beneficial owner's jurisdiction. Denial of treaty relief, the lifting of the corporate veil, retroactive cancellation of tax rulings, and penalties of up to three times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally jointly and severally liable for group taxes, social security contributions, and customs duties where assets were stripped and the company was operated as an instrument of fraud. Travel bans and asset freezes can arise under Swiss tax enforcement and cross-border mutual assistance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-provision of local file, master file, or country-by-country report within 30 days of a Swiss tax audit request, or failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation for cross-border purchases and trading with related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ad hoc penalties for non-compliance with documentation obligations can amount to CHF 10,000 or more. The tax authority may apply a rebuttable presumption adjusting the taxpayer's profit to the disadvantage of the company, plus interest and possible penalty tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable if they intentionally or negligently fail to maintain required accounting and TP records; a director's personal liability to the company for breach of fiduciary duty extends to the resulting tax savings reversed by the assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or deemed dividends to foreign shareholders without deducting and remitting the 35% Swiss anticipatory tax or without establishing treaty relief at source. This includes disguised loans, excessive royalty payments, or capital reductions with pre-distribution profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withheld anticipatory tax is recoverable from the company together with interest (3.5% p.a.). Failure to declare taxable distributions triggers tax evasion penalties. Repeated non-compliance may result in the tax administration demanding a security deposit prior to future distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company directors are jointly and severally liable to pay the unremitted withholding tax, penalties and interest if they knowingly or negligently ordered the transfer without tax clearance. Personal liability may reach the full distribution amount if liquidity has already been transferred abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Swiss private banking relationships to structure payments from the dehydrated spice export trade through shell entities or to third countries without genuine commercial purpose, or failing to comply with Swiss AML due diligence for cash-based/OTC transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the Swiss AMLA for financial intermediaries and, if the AG is a licensed financial institution, penalties up to CHF 1 million or more; criminal sanctions include imprisonment equal to the gravity of the offence. Business operations can be suspended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with managerial responsibility face criminal liability for money laundering under the Swiss Criminal Code (Art. 305bis/305ter), including imprisonment and substantial personal fines. The civil liability extends to compensation for damages and the dissolution of the entity.
